title: The nuclear atom and alpha-particle scattering practice

evidence_basis.originality_note: Original foil, detector and model contexts test the mapped inference and property-identification demands without copying official wording, values or diagrams.

questions.prompt: Describe the simple nuclear model of an atom. Include the locations and charges of protons, neutrons and electrons.
In a thin-foil experiment, most alpha particles pass through with little or no deflection. What is the best inference?

options.A: Most of the atom is empty space.
options.C: Electrons contain nearly all the atomic mass.
options.D: The nucleus occupies most of the atom's volume.

questions.prompt: A positively charged alpha particle is deflected through a large angle as it passes through metal foil. Which feature of the atom caused the deflection?

options.A: A large region of negative charge spread through the atom
options.B: A small region of concentrated positive charge
options.C: A neutron orbiting outside the nucleus
options.D: An empty region with no electric interaction

questions.prompt: Which row correctly describes the simple nuclear atom?

options.A: Protons and electrons in the nucleus; neutrons orbit outside
options.B: Neutrons in the nucleus; protons and electrons orbit outside
options.C: Protons and neutrons in the nucleus; electrons orbit outside
options.D: Electrons in the nucleus; protons and neutrons orbit outside

questions.prompt: A detector records the paths of alpha particles after they cross a thin metal foil.

figure.purpose: Assess interpretation of the frequency and size of alpha-particle deflections.
figure.brief: Original black-and-white Cambridge-inspired track diagram. Show 100 representative incoming paths: 94 straight or nearly straight, 5 at modest angles and 1 through a large angle. Label groups P, Q and R but include no atomic model or inference text.
figure.alt_text: Most alpha-particle tracks continue straight, several bend modestly and one bends through a large angle.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: State what the paths in group P suggest about the volume of the atom.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Explain what the path in group R suggests about the charge, size and mass distribution of the nucleus.

questions.prompt: A student draws a model with a large nucleus filling half the atom. The nucleus contains protons and neutrons, and electrons are outside it.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Identify two features of the model that agree with the simple nuclear atom.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Use alpha-particle scattering evidence to explain why the drawn size of the nucleus is not acceptable.

questions.prompt: Three alpha particles approach an atom along the paths shown.

figure.purpose: Assess closest-approach reasoning and construction of a complete evidence-based nuclear model.
figure.brief: Original black-and-white Cambridge-inspired sketch. Show a faint circular atomic boundary and a tiny unlabelled central point. Path X passes far from the point, Y passes moderately close and Z heads almost directly toward it. Stop all three paths before their outcomes so learners can predict them. Do not show electrons or charge signs.
figure.alt_text: Three alpha-particle paths approach an atom at far, moderate and very close distances from a tiny unlabelled centre.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Predict and compare the deflections of X, Y and Z.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Explain why particle Z is repelled rather than attracted when it approaches the centre.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: State where the protons, neutrons and electrons are located in the atom shown.
